tasks.spec:
You are an Elixir/OTP engineer porting the `run` command of a Python CLI to Elixir, matching its observable behaviour byte for byte. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the Cornerman repo, an Elixir/OTP port of the Ringer agent-swarm tool. Edit files here directly.

NEVER TOUCH: anything under test/ (the conformance tests are the acceptance check), DIVERGENCES.toml (the ledger of accepted differences; you may not add entries), bin/, mix.exs, mix.lock, vendor/, .git. Do not git commit, push or git add. Do not add dependencies: use Elixir's built-in JSON module, the declared toml_elixir (TomlElixir.decode/1), erlexec (only through Cornerman.Spawn) and phoenix_pubsub.

OWNED PATHS (the only files you may create or edit): anything under lib/cornerman/, plus ./notes.md. That includes extending the existing boundary modules (Manifest, AppConfig, Lint, CLI, CLI.Args). Cornerman.Spawn (lib/cornerman/spawn.ex, lib/cornerman/spawn/) may gain ADDITIVE options (for example an :env option), but its existing behaviour must not change: the phase 0 tests in test/cornerman/spawn_test.exs must stay green.

GOAL: `bin/cornerman run <manifest.json> [--max-parallel N] [--identity ID] [--no-dashboard] [--browser] [--no-artifact] [--dry-run] [--allow-noncanonical-route]` (plus the global `--config PATH`) must behave exactly like `ringer.py run`: same exit status, same stdout and stderr, and the same files afterwards (the run state JSON under <state_dir>/runs/, runs.jsonl eval rows, ~/.ringer/active-runs.json, the artifact library <state_dir>/artifacts/library.json and the artifact file set, harvested deliverables, worker.log files, task directories), before and after normalisation of run ids, timestamps, pids and durations. The harness is test/support/scenario.ex (read its moduledoc: fixtures, normalisation, the same-home rule, the live snapshot); the cases are test/conformance/run_test.exs; the lint cases in test/conformance/lint_test.exs must stay green. Two ledger entries apply: (1) HTML files (live status page, final report, version page, runs index, the view/ file wrappers) must exist at exactly the oracle's paths, but their contents are not compared until phase 3 renders them from HEEx, so write a small, valid, honest HTML page for each (run name, task table with status/verdict, links to deliverables/logs); (2) for an unparseable config.toml the text after `cornerman: error: ` may be the Elixir TOML parser's message.

PROGRAM NAME: Cornerman prints `cornerman` where Ringer's CLI text names itself for a human: `cornerman: error: ...`, `usage: cornerman run ...`, and `run 'cornerman models'` / `run 'cornerman hud'` in the closing lines (Ringer prints './ringer.py models'). Everything on the data plane stays byte-identical to Ringer, because Ringside, the models scoreboard and backfill scripts read it: the `[ringer.py]` markers in worker logs and check output, eval-row values shepherd_model "none (ringer.py)" and pattern "ringer-py", and so on.

THE REFERENCE is the Python source at /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py/ringer.py. Read these before writing code and port their behaviour exactly, including message text, ordering, rounding and edge cases:
- CLI: build_parser (10866; the run subparser at 10890) and main (11090; the path from `config = AppConfig.load` at 11152 through run_manifest at 11214, and the error handling at its end). argparse's own usage/error output for `run` is compared too.
- Config: AppConfig.load (1078) and what it reads: state_dir, identity_default, allow_full_access, [eval] (load_eval_config 1545: backend, jsonl_path), [artifact] (load_artifact_config 1043), engines (load_engines 1645, built_in_codex_engine 1523: bin, args_template, sandbox_args, full_access_args, model_default, token_regex, model_report_regex, process_name). print_engine_bin_diagnostics runs for `run` (the lint port already has the diagnostics; reuse them).
- Before any worker: print_steering_notes (9634; a no-op without [steering], leave steering itself to a later phase), lint_manifest (1901) now WITH include_model_log_nudges=True and config (the task_type nudge; noncanonical_route_findings 6447 with config), `ERROR:` findings abort with exit 1; validate_manifest_engines (9710); resolve_identity (9491) and find_repo_identity (9470) with the manifest's workdir and directory as start paths; --no-artifact; dry_run (10104); preflight_engine_bins (9686).
- The run: run_manifest (10629) with register_active_run/unregister_active_run (3275, 3295; read/prune/write of active-runs.json at ringer_home() = $RINGER_HOME), RingerRunner (8770-9424): taskdir and log path rules (_taskdir 9408, _log_path 9415, the worker.log unlink at start), _run_task (8863: slots, attempts, statuses running/retrying/verifying/pass/fail, the retry spec text built by build_failure_context 9943 from tail_text 9766), _prepare_taskdir (8976, the non-worktree branch; worktrees mode is phase 2b), _record_prepare_error (9066), _run_worker (9090: engine lookup and full_access errors, build_worker_command 9597, the log lines with shell_command_for_display and redact_spec, tee of raw worker output bytes to the log AND to the CLI's stdout as they arrive, the 1,000,000-byte capture tail, timeout, parse_token_count 9528, parse_reported_model 9550), Verifier (8704: check via `sh -c` in the taskdir with the 60 s CHECK_TIMEOUT_S, missing expect_files message, the silent-failure message, output[:2000]), verdict_for (9452), _log_attempt (9258: every eval-row field, the notes text, resolved_task_model 9585, effective_reasoning_effort_from_command 9572, the identity mismatch log line), _harvest_deliverables_on_pass (8914: expect_files, the fallback harvest with FALLBACK_HARVEST_SUFFIXES and the 8-file cap note, the 20 MB limit, copies into artifacts/deliverables/<run_id>/<task>/), build_run_id (9462), print_summary (10174), and the closing lines in RingerRunner.run's finally block (8843-8850).
- EvalLogger (5847; the jsonl backend and the fields it adds: logged_at, log_sink, fallback_reason).
- StateWriter (2272-2573): every field of snapshot (2360), including activity (worker_activity 9812 and helpers), log_tail/log_tail_full (tail_lines 9737), children (ProcessTree 2219), elapsed_s rounding, totals, summary, report_ready, artifact_path/live_path/report_path; the start/finish/stop order and the final re-flush with report_ready. atomic_write_text/atomic_write_json (2575): JSON with indent=2, sort_keys, trailing newline.
- The artifact library and file set: artifacts_dir .. reconcile_artifact_library_dead_runs (3301-3500: library.json, live/<run_name>.html, versions/<run_name>/<run_id>.html, pruning), collect_state_deliverables (4347), ArtifactRenderer.link_for_source / wrapper_path / write_wrapper (4229-4287, which decide which view/<run_id>/<task>--<file>.html wrappers exist), and the index page path. Match which files exist and library.json exactly; HTML contents are yours.

DESIGN (from the project plan; the cold review checks it): the run subtree must be host-agnostic, because phase 3 hosts the same subtree in a daemon. Put the run under a Runs DynamicSupervisor: one Run supervisor per run with a Run.Server (a GenServer that owns the queue, hands out max_parallel slots and keeps the run summary the exit code comes from) and a supervisor for the per-task processes. Each task is a `:gen_statem` (Cornerman.Run.TaskLifecycle or similar) started with restart: :temporary, with states queued -> preparing -> running -> verifying -> passed | failed. timeout_s and the 60 s check timeout are gen_statem timeouts, not sleeps. A domain retry (the check failed and attempts remain) is an explicit verifying -> running transition that carries the failure context into the next prompt; it is never a supervisor restart, and an illegal transition must crash rather than write a bad status. Workers and checks run only through Cornerman.Spawn (process groups, kill on timeout). Every transition is published on Phoenix.PubSub (start it in the application; topic per run id). A StateMirror process subscribes and writes the state JSON atomically (a temp file in the same directory, then rename) on every event and on a 1-second timer for elapsed time, log tails and child counts. An EvalLog process owns the runs.jsonl append. active-runs.json is written as a projection at run start and end. Validate at the boundary: manifest and config become validated structs in their modules; the state machine never handles malformed input. The CLI stays a thin dispatcher: it validates, starts the run, streams worker output to stdout, waits for the result and prints the summary; the run subtree itself never calls System.halt or writes to the terminal except through the output sink the CLI gives it. Dashboards: accept --no-dashboard and --browser, but start no per-run dashboard and no HUD (they are retired or phase 3); port and dashboard_port stay null. Do not implement the catalog auto-refresh, steering injection, worktrees, --baseline, demo, ask or signal handling: later slices.

SETUP (run once, first, from this directory; the sandbox cannot fetch packages and this worktree has no submodule checkout):
  cp -R /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/deps ./deps
  export PATH=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/elixir/1.20.1-otp-28/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/erlang/28.5/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin:$PATH HEX_OFFLINE=1 CORNERMAN_ORACLE=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py CORNERMAN_PYTHON=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3

HOW TO RUN (after the setup, from this directory):
  MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format
  mix test test/conformance/run_test.exs              # all run cases; a failure names the field or file that differs
  mix test test/conformance/run_test.exs:<line>       # one case
  CORNERMAN_SELF_CHECK=1 mix test test/conformance/run_test.exs   # oracle vs oracle: proves the harness, must always pass
  mix test                                             # everything: lint, run, spawn
  RINGER_NO_SELF_UPDATE=1 RINGER_NO_CATALOG_REFRESH=1 /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3 /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py/ringer.py run --no-dashboard --identity me <manifest>   # what the oracle does
To see a whole observation, call Cornerman.Conformance.Scenario.run_both/1 from a script with `MIX_ENV=test mix run <script.exs>` and inspect the maps. Iterate until `mix test` passes in full. The verifying check runs outside your sandbox against the same oracle, from clean dependencies, twice, and fails if any fake worker or `sleep` process outlives the suite.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: the port under lib/cornerman/, formatted, compiling with no warnings, plus ./notes.md with: your process and module layout and why, how a task moves through the gen_statem (including the retry transition), every Python behaviour you found surprising or had to emulate (rounding, repr, ordering, truncation, byte handling), the final test result line, anything your sandboxed test run could not exercise, and any conformance case you believe is wrong, with the reason. Never edit a test, the ledger, bin/ or the mix files to make a case pass.
tasks.verified: every run and lint conformance case matches the pinned Ringer oracle (twice, outside the sandbox, from clean deps), no worker outlives the suite, tests/ledger/launcher/mix files untouched, only lib/cornerman changed, formatted, no warnings.
